questions.question: A rectangular card is divided into 4 equal parts, and every part has one sticker on it. The first part has a closed shape made of 3 straight sides. The second part has a closed shape made of 4 straight sides. The third part has a closed shape made of one curved line all the way around. The fourth part has a closed shape made of 5 straight sides. How many of the 4 parts hold a polygon?
options: 3 parts
4 parts, because every part holds a closed shape
2 parts
1 part
questions.explain: A polygon must be closed AND made of straight sides only, so the 3-sided, 4-sided and 5-sided shapes count — that is 3 parts. The common trap is counting the shape made of a curved line, but a curved shape is never a polygon.

questions.question: A rectangular ribbon is divided into 5 equal parts. 3 of those parts are shaded, and each shaded part holds one closed shape made of 5 straight sides. What is the name of the shape inside each shaded part?
options: Quadrilateral
Pentagon
Hexagon
Circle, because the shape closes all the way around
questions.explain: We name a polygon by counting its straight sides: 5 straight sides means pentagon (4 sides is a quadrilateral, 6 is a hexagon). Being closed is not enough to make a shape round — the choice that says circle forgets that a circle has no straight sides at all.

questions.question: A rectangular placemat is divided into 3 equal parts. The left part holds a closed shape made of 4 straight sides. The middle part holds a closed shape made of 1 straight side and 1 curved side. The right part holds a path of 3 straight sides that do not join up, so the shape stays open. Which part holds a polygon?
options: The middle part
The middle part and the left part
The left part
All three parts
questions.explain: Only the left part works: 4 straight sides, all joined and closed, so it is a quadrilateral. The half-round shape in the middle is out because one side is curved, and the right part is out because an open path is not a polygon.

questions.question: A rectangular poster is divided into 8 equal parts. 5 of the parts are shaded, and each shaded part holds a closed shape made of 8 straight sides. The other 3 parts are unshaded, and each one holds a round shape with no straight sides at all. How many parts of the poster hold a polygon?
options: 8, all of them
questions.explain: The 5 shaded parts each hold an octagon (8 straight sides), so 5 parts hold polygons. The trap is counting the 3 round shapes as well — a shape with no straight sides can never be a polygon, no matter how neatly it closes.

questions.question: A shape is closed and is made only of straight sides. It has 7 vertices. What is this shape called?
options: A heptagon
An octagon
A hexagon, because 7 vertices make only 6 sides
It is not a polygon, because it has an odd number of sides
questions.explain: In a closed straight-sided shape the number of vertices always equals the number of sides, so 7 vertices means 7 sides — a heptagon. Odd or even makes no difference; only 'closed' and 'all sides straight' decide whether it is a polygon.

questions.question: Nico sorts stickers for his SkyTrain scrapbook. He has a stop-sign sticker with 8 straight sides, a yield-sign sticker with 3 straight sides, a moon sticker made of 2 curved sides, and a ticket sticker with 4 straight sides. Which group holds polygons only?
options: All four stickers
The stop-sign sticker, the yield-sign sticker and the ticket sticker
The moon sticker and the stop-sign sticker
The yield-sign sticker and the moon sticker
questions.explain: The stop sign is an octagon, the yield sign is a triangle and the ticket is a quadrilateral — all closed with straight sides only. Any group that keeps the moon sticker is wrong, because its curved sides leave it out of the polygon family.

questions.question: A closed shape is made of 6 straight sides. Every side measures 4 cm and every vertex is the same. Which statement about this shape is true?
options: It is a pentagon, because 6 equal sides meet at only 5 vertices
It is not a polygon, because all of its sides are equal
It is a regular hexagon
It is a regular circle
questions.explain: Count the straight sides to name it: 6 sides means hexagon, and because all sides and vertices are equal it is a regular hexagon. Equal sides never disqualify a shape, and the word 'regular' cannot rescue a circle — a circle has no straight sides, so it is not a polygon.

questions.question: Which description names a quadrilateral?
options: A closed shape with 4 straight sides and 1 curved side
An open path made of 4 straight sides
A closed shape with 4 curved sides
A closed shape with 4 straight sides and 4 vertices
questions.explain: A quadrilateral is closed, has 4 straight sides and therefore 4 vertices. Adding even one curved side, or leaving the path open, means the shape is not a polygon at all — so it cannot be named for its sides.

questions.question: Aria builds a border all the way around a garden bed at her Surrey school. She uses straight boards, one board for each side: 3 boards that are 2 m long and 4 boards that are 1 m long. The border joins up completely and no board is curved. What is the name of the shape her border makes?
options: A heptagon
An octagon
A hexagon, because two of the short boards join into one side
It is not a polygon, because the sides are not all the same length
questions.explain: First count the sides: 3 + 4 = 7 boards, so 7 straight sides, which makes a heptagon. Sides of different lengths only mean the polygon is irregular — a polygon does not need equal sides, it needs to be closed with every side straight.

questions.question: On a classroom poster there is a half-moon shape made of 1 straight side and 1 curved side, joined so the shape is closed. Ravi says it is a polygon because it is closed and it has a straight side. Why is Ravi wrong?
options: Ravi is right, because a closed shape with at least one straight side is a polygon
A polygon must have every side straight, and this shape has a curved side
Ravi is wrong, because a polygon must have all of its sides the same length
Ravi is wrong, because a polygon must have more than 4 sides
questions.explain: A polygon needs both attributes: closed AND every single side straight. Having one straight side is not enough, which is exactly the mistake with the half-moon; and polygons do not need equal sides or a minimum of 5 sides — a triangle with three different sides is still a polygon.

questions.question: A quilt block for a BC art fair uses 12 fabric pieces: 5 triangles, 4 pieces with 4 straight sides each, 2 round pieces with no straight sides, and 1 closed piece with 5 straight sides. How many pieces are polygons, and which polygon has the most sides?
options: 12 polygons, and a round piece has the most sides
10 polygons, and a triangle has the most sides
10 polygons, and the pentagon has the most sides
12 polygons, and the pentagon has the most sides
questions.explain: Step one: 5 + 4 + 1 = 10 straight-sided closed pieces are polygons, and the 2 round pieces are not. Step two: compare side counts — 5 beats 4 and 3, so the pentagon has the most sides; counting all 12 pieces is the usual slip.

questions.question: A designer starts a hockey-rink logo as a closed shape with 4 straight sides. Then she replaces one of the straight sides with a curved arc, and the shape still joins up all the way around. What is true about the new shape?
options: It is still a quadrilateral, because it still has 4 sides
It becomes a regular polygon, because the curve makes it smoother
It becomes a triangle, because only 3 straight sides are left
It is no longer a polygon, because one of its sides is curved
questions.explain: Once any side is curved, the shape stops being a polygon, so it has no side-name at all — not a quadrilateral and not a triangle. Staying closed is only half the rule; the other half is that every side must be straight.
